answers.label: Feedback on clarified MBM definition
answers.text: We have concerns about introducing strict hourly matching rule into the MBM. Carbon credit markets do not require such matching, and their flexibility could make them more attractive than Renewable Energy Certificate (REC). This could unintentionally shift corporate away from GHG-P and REC system toward voluntary/local guidance and carbon credit system, spoiling GHG-P’s role as a unified global standard.

answers.label: Feedback on stated purposes of the MBM
answers.text: The proposed hourly matching requirement may impose significant gidital and operational burdens on power generators, brokers, and off-takers. Increased computational burden could even raise global electricity consumption and hence CO2 emission. The purpose of this revision should be to deliver clear and measurable CO2 reductions that outweigh the increase by computational burden. Until such benefit is clearly demonstrated, hourly matching should be framed as “may” or “should”, instead of “shall.”

answers.label: Comments on opposition to QC4
answers.text: The treatment of REC vintage under hourly matching system is unclear. For example, can a REC generated at 1 am on 1st January 2029 be applied to consumption at 1 am on 1st January 2030? If REC with past vintage is not usable and only live REC is allowed, finding REC with very specific vintage in the market is tough work. Can you find a wine bottle which was produced at the exactly same timing as your birth, in the market? Such strict rule on vintage would delay GHG calculation and reporting timeline, significantly.

answers.text: To ensure practical implementation, GHG Protocol should align rules with I-REC secretariat. answers.label: Resources that should not qualify as SSS
answers.text: CAPEX subsidies for renewable power generators should be excluded from SSS examples. Three reasons: (1) Subsidies do not make the Government nor Taxpayers the project owner. The recipient of subsidy remains the owner of the renewable power plants. (2) Tax Incentive for CAPEC of renewable power plants is not SSS, though tax incentive and subsidy are similar. (3) Fossil and Nuclear power plants have historically relied heavily on Governmental supports; so, scrutinizing only renewable subsidies is unfair.
